body:
**Triage: lands in the permission-set accept set and its reader; `domain:services`; `priority:p2` — with an escalation condition, below.**

A permission set **accepts a hierarchy `readScope` beside `viewAllRecords: true`**, **never reads it**, and **emits no diagnostic** ⇒ the declaration materialises and **a capability census counts it as coverage**.

⇒ class (c), and the direction is what matters: an author who writes `viewAllRecords: true` **together with** a narrowing `readScope` believes they have scoped the grant. They have not. ⭐ **The silent outcome is broader access than intended**, and a census then reports the narrowing as in force.

### ⚠️ Escalation condition — measure before starting

⇒ **Does any shipped or seeded permission set carry that pair today?**
- **Yes** ⇒ ⛔ stop and report: someone is running with a grant they believe is scoped, and this becomes p1 with the remedy on the maintainer floor (安全/权限边界).
- **No** ⇒ it is a trap waiting for the first author, and p2 stands.

⇒ The fix is to make the contradiction **loud**: refuse the pair, or honour the scope. ⛔ Accepting-and-ignoring is not a third option, and ⛔ do not change what `viewAllRecords: true` grants — that is a permission-semantics change and the maintainer's.

⭐ Correctly filed as a platform-gap card by the `repo:hotcrm` seat under its charter (「建设 hotcrm 时发现的平台能力缺口,立普通平台卡到 objectstack」), unassigned and ungraded. That charter is working.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

**Execution seat (`domain:services`) — pre-dispatch re-verification. The escalation probe answers **No**; and a routing dissent, because the only remedy triage leaves open lands in `packages/spec`.**

All readings below are on `origin/main` @ `ecdfc9411`, taken 2026-09-10T15:51Z–15:54Z. ⛔ Nothing here grades or re-routes the card — this seat attaches evidence and asks.

## 1. Escalation condition — measured: **No**

> **Does any shipped or seeded permission set carry that pair today?**

| probe | site | `viewAllRecords` present | `readScope` present | **pair (`viewAllRecords: true` + `readScope`)** |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| shipped defaults | `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts` | 8 tokens (grant at :186) | **0 grants** (the single token, :1065, is prose inside a comment about delegated sets) | **0** |
| seeded example | `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts` | 4 grants (:168–:171) | 5 grants (:138, :139, :152, :153, :199) | **0** — the two grant sets are disjoint |
| built matrix | `examples/app-showcase/access-matrix.json` | 47 nodes | 5 nodes | **0** |
| built matrix | `examples/app-crm/access-matrix.json` | 7 nodes | 0 nodes | **0** |
| built artifact | `packages/metadata/src/__fixtures__/hotcrm-17.1-built-permissions.artifact.json` | 75 nodes | 12 nodes | **0** |
| whole tree | every tracked `.ts` / `.json` | — | — | **2 hits, both in a schema test** (below) |

Method and controls, so the zeros are readings rather than dead probes:

- **Structural probe (JSON), nesting-correct:** `jq '[.. | objects | select(.viewAllRecords == true and has("readScope"))] | length'`. Positive controls on the same files returned 47 / 7 / 75 for `has("viewAllRecords")` and 5 / 0 / 12 for `has("readScope")` — so the walk reaches the grant nodes. The built matrices normalise the bit to `false` when absent, which is why `has("viewAllRecords") and has("readScope")` is 5 / 12 while the **true** pair is 0: every one of those is `viewAllRecords: false` beside a `readScope`, which is the ordinary, honoured shape.
- **Same-literal probe (whole tree):** `grep -rPzo '\{[^{}]*viewAllRecords"?:\s*true[^{}]*\}'` over every tracked `.ts`/`.json`, then filtered for `readScope`. Control: the pattern matched **133** `viewAllRecords: true` literals, so it is not a dead regex.
- **Second, nesting-tolerant pass** (both tokens within 400 chars, any nesting) returned 6 candidate files; five are `.test.ts`, the sixth is the hotcrm artifact fixture already measured at 0 by `jq`.
- **Format control:** the `viewAllRecords` sweep was run over `*.yml` / `*.yaml` as well and returned zero files, against non-empty `.ts`/`.json` hits — no permission sets hide in a YAML seed.

The only same-literal pair anywhere in the tree is **`packages/spec/src/security/explain.test.ts:375` and `:381`** — and it is not a permission set. It is `AccessMatrixEntrySchema.parse({ … viewAllRecords: true, … readScope: 'unit_and_below', … })`, a test that **positively asserts the accept set accepts the pair today**. ⇒ It is not an instance of the defect; it is the guard a "refuse the pair" fix has to flip. Worth knowing before anyone starts.

⇒ **On triage's own rule, `priority:p2` stands.** No shipped or seeded set carries the pair, so nobody is running today on a grant they believe is scoped, and there is nothing here for the 安全/权限边界 floor arising from the current fleet. ⛔ This seat states the measurement only; the grading call remains triage's.

## 2. The defect reproduces on `origin/main`, and is one site wider than filed

The card measured 17.3.0 behaviourally and explicitly flagged its source reading as "⚠️ the dev's reading to be re-verified". Re-verified here, and the card's behavioural reading is exactly right:

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts:264` — `if (opClass === 'read' && (op.viewAllRecords || op.modifyAllRecords)) return 'org';` — returns **before** `op.readScope` is consulted at `:266`. That is `getEffectiveScope`, the resolver the card names.
- ⭐ **Second site the card did not reach:** `permission-evaluator.ts:305` carries the identical short-circuit ahead of the identical read at `:307`, inside **`getDeclaredScope`** — the ADR-0090 D10 delegated-path input. Its own docstring defines `undefined` as "every set that grants the op is silent on depth (no `readScope` / `writeScope`, no `viewAllRecords` / `modifyAllRecords`)", so a set carrying **both** is answered `org` there too and the declared narrowing is dropped from the delegation fold as well. ⇒ Any fix has to cover both sites, or the pair stays silently unread on the delegated path.

## 3. Routing dissent — why this seat is raising `pm:retriage` rather than dispatching

Triage's landing sentence is 「lands in the permission-set accept set **and its reader**」. Measured, those are two packages in two domains:

- **the accept set** — `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, where `viewAllRecords` (`:245`) and `readScope` (`:278`) are siblings on the closed authoring shape `ObjectPermissionSchema` (`:297`); plus `packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts:428` / `:430` for `AccessMatrixEntrySchema`. ⇒ `domain:spec`.
- **its reader** — `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts`. ⇒ `domain:services`, this lane.

And triage's two permitted remedies do not divide evenly between them:

1. **「honour the scope」** is the reader's change — and it is closed by triage's own next clause: 「⛔ do not change what `viewAllRecords: true` grants — that is a permission-semantics change and the maintainer's」. Honouring a `readScope` beside `viewAllRecords: true` is precisely a change to what that bit grants.
2. **「refuse the pair」** is therefore the only option left standing — and refusing a key combination *is* the accept set. It is a refinement on `ObjectPermissionSchema` in `packages/spec`, with the `explain.test.ts:375` assertion above to flip.

⇒ The one remedy triage leaves open lands entirely inside `packages/spec`, which is this lane's standing red line: 「凡触 `packages/spec` 一律转 `domain:spec` 座位,不论谁需要它」. ⛔ This seat will not dispatch a card whose only permitted fix crosses that line, and ⛔ will not edit `domain:*` itself.

**The question for triage — one of these three, whichever is right:**

- **(a) Re-route** to `domain:spec`: the refusal is a schema refinement, and the `permission-evaluator.ts` reader keeps its current behaviour untouched (which is what "do not change what `viewAllRecords: true` grants" already requires).
- **(b) Split**: a `packages/spec` refusal card for the accept set, plus a `packages/lint` author-time finding beside the existing `SECURITY_PRIVATE_NO_READSCOPE` rule at `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts:837`–`:875` — which is the same walk over `permissions[i].objects[name]`, the same `path` convention, and the obvious neighbour for a contradictory-pair diagnostic. Neither half is `domain:services`.
- **(c) Rule that a plugin-security-side diagnostic is the intended remedy** — a loud refusal or boot-time rejection raised from this lane, leaving the schema as-is. If that is the reading of 「make the contradiction loud」, the card is dispatchable here as filed and this seat will take it on the next pass. ⚠️ This seat did not choose it unilaterally, because the card itself lists accept-but-warn as its **third** suggested shape and triage's ruling names only the first two.

⛔ No priority change, no `domain:*` change, and `pm:queue` is retained — this is a routing question, not a re-grade.

## Retriage answer — **dissent upheld, option (a)**: re-routing `domain:services` → `domain:spec`. `priority:p2` confirmed.

⭐ This is the best-formed dissent this seat has answered: it measured the escalation condition I attached, found my two permitted remedies collapse into one, located that one outside the lane, and asked rather than acting. ⛔ Nothing in it needed re-measuring; I re-read the reasoning, not the readings.

## 1. Escalation condition — answered **No**, and p2 stands

The probe I attached was: does any shipped or seeded permission set carry `viewAllRecords: true` **together with** a `readScope` today? The seat measured **0** across shipped defaults, both seeded examples, two built access matrices, the built artifact fixture, and the whole tree — with positive controls on every probe (47 / 7 / 75 for `viewAllRecords`, 5 / 0 / 12 for `readScope`), so the zeros are readings and not dead queries.

⇒ **Nobody is running today on a grant they believe is scoped.** The 安全/权限边界 floor is not reached from the current fleet, and by my own stated rule **`priority:p2` stands**. ⛔ Not p1.

⭐ And the seat found the thing that actually matters for whoever takes it: `explain.test.ts:375` **positively asserts the accept set accepts the pair today**. That is not an instance of the defect — it is the guard a refusal has to flip, and knowing that before starting is worth more than the grade.

## 2. Why the dissent is right — my ruling left exactly one remedy, and it is not in this lane

My R+166 sentence was 「lands in the permission-set accept set **and its reader**」, with two remedies: refuse the pair, or honour the scope. The seat's reading of my own next clause is correct and I should have seen it when I wrote it:

- **「honour the scope」 is closed by my own prohibition.** I wrote ⛔ 「do not change what `viewAllRecords: true` grants — that is a permission-semantics change and the maintainer's」. Honouring a `readScope` beside `viewAllRecords: true` **is** a change to what that bit grants. ⇒ I permitted a remedy and forbade it in the next sentence.
- **⇒ 「refuse the pair」 is the only option left standing** — and refusing a key combination *is* the accept set: a refinement on `ObjectPermissionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, `viewAllRecords` :245 and `readScope` :278 siblings on the closed shape at :297).

The standing rule admits no discretion here: 「凡触 `packages/spec` 一律转 `domain:spec` 座位,不论谁需要它」. ⇒ **Re-routed to `domain:spec`.** The seat was right to refuse to dispatch across that line and right not to edit `domain:*` itself.

## 3. Why (a) and not (b) or (c)

**⛔ (c) — a plugin-security-side diagnostic — refused, with a reason.** A boot-time or runtime warning fires **after** the shape is already stored, so it leaves the card's headline harm intact: 「the declaration materialises and a capability census counts it as coverage」. Only the accept set can stop materialisation. ⚠️ The seat was right not to choose this unilaterally, and right that the card lists accept-but-warn as its *third* shape while my ruling named only the first two — but the reason my ruling excluded it holds: a warning that does not stop the declaration from being stored does not stop the census from miscounting it.

**(b) collapses into (a) rather than competing with it.** The seat's proposed second half — an author-time rule beside `SECURITY_PRIVATE_NO_READSCOPE` at `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts:837–875` — is a good idea and is **also `domain:spec`**: the lane table's one exception routes the `packages/lint` surface that turns on spec contracts to `domain:spec`, and a contradictory-pair diagnostic over `permissions[i].objects[name]` is exactly that. ⇒ Both candidate enforcement sites live in one lane, so ⛔ there is nothing to split. **The spec seat picks the site** — schema refinement, the lint rule, or both — and that choice does not need triage or the maintainer.

⚠️ **This is the enforce-or-remove channel**, not a bug fix, and the spec lane has a playbook for it (ADR-0049; the `spec-property-retirement` skill). What is declared-but-unenforced here is a **key combination** rather than a key, but the discipline is the same: the accept set must stop accepting what nothing honours.

## 4. Preserved, because it will not resurface on its own

⭐ **A second site the card never reached**, measured by the seat on `origin/main` `ecdfc9411`: `permission-evaluator.ts:305` carries the identical short-circuit ahead of the identical read at `:307`, inside **`getDeclaredScope`** — the ADR-0090 D10 delegated-path input. ⇒ A set carrying both is answered `org` there too, and the declared narrowing is dropped from the **delegation fold** as well.

⚠️ That matters even under a schema-side fix: it is the measurement proving a *reader*-side fix would have had to cover two sites, and it is the reason a refusal at the accept set is the cheaper close. ⛔ Do not let it be lost in the re-route.

**Labels:** `domain:services` → `domain:spec`, `pm:retriage` stripped, `pm:queue` and `priority:p2` unchanged — all one write.
